B: Which RNA component typically pairs with a bacterial Shine–Dalgarno element?
23S rRNA
16S rRNA
5S rRNA
Initiator tRNA anticodon
16S rRNA belongs to the small subunit and contains the anti-SD region. 23S rRNA contributes to peptide-bond catalysis; the anticodon recognizes the start codon, not the SD motif.
Which arrangement describes an elongation-ready bacterial initiation complex?
fMet-tRNA in A; next codon in P
Uncharged initiator in E
fMet-tRNA in P; next codon in A
Two elongator tRNAs in A and P
The first donor occupies P directly; the next aminoacyl-tRNA enters A during elongation. Neither an uncharged initiator nor an already assembled pair of elongator tRNAs describes this endpoint.
Which factor has a defining GTPase role during bacterial initiation?
IF1
IF3
EF-G
IF2
IF2 uses GTP during initiation-complex maturation. IF1 and IF3 are not initiation GTPases; EF-G acts principally during translocation and recycling.
A bacterial GUG is successfully selected as an initiation codon. What is usually installed first?
N-formylmethionine
Valine
Glycine
Leucine
GUG specifies valine internally, but a genuine bacterial initiation GUG is decoded by the initiator methionine tRNA, usually formylated.
Which donor supplies the formyl group to bacterial Met-tRNAf?
S-adenosylmethionine
10-formyltetrahydrofolate
Acetyl-CoA
ATP
Methionyl-tRNA formyltransferase transfers a one-carbon formyl group from 10-formyl-THF. SAM transfers methyl groups in other reactions; ATP activates methionine during charging.
Which statement about methionyl-tRNA synthetase in the typical E. coli system is correct?
It charges only the elongator species
It attaches preformed fMet
It charges both initiator and elongator tRNAs with Met
It catalyzes IF2 GTP hydrolysis
The usual MetRS recognizes both methionine tRNA classes. The initiator is formylated afterward by a separate enzyme; IF2 has its own GTPase activity.
IF1 is most directly associated with which region during initiation?
Large-subunit peptide exit tunnel
DNA promoter
E-site exit channel exclusively
Small-subunit A-site region
IF1 occupies the A-region and helps organize an initiation-specific state. It is not a transcription factor or a peptide-processing enzyme.
Which factor contributes prominently to rejecting unsuitable initiation complexes and opposing premature subunit joining?
IF3
EF-Tu
Peptide deformylase
Methionyl-tRNA synthetase
IF3 acts on the 30S subunit to promote fidelity and regulate association. EF-Tu delivers elongator tRNA; the enzymes modify or charge substrates.
Which is the antiparallel complement of 5′-AGGAGG-3′ as written underneath it?
5′-UCCUCC-3′
3′-UCCUCC-5′
3′-AGGAGG-5′
5′-AGGAGG-3′
The two strands of an ordinary RNA duplex run antiparallel and pair A with U, G with C. If written 5′→3′ the complement would be CCUCCU.
Why does a stronger SD duplex not invariably yield a higher initiation rate?
The SD motif encodes fMet
SD pairing requires DNA
Spacing, accessibility and later release can constrain productive initiation
16S RNA is absent from 30S
The pathway requires more than association. An inaccessible motif, mispositioned codon or slow subsequent rearrangement can negate favorable pairing.
Which event marks completion of canonical initiation rather than the beginning of elongation?
First peptide bond
EF-G translocation
Release of a completed chain
Factor-cleared 70S complex with initiator positioned in P
The first peptide bond occurs after the next aminoacyl-tRNA is selected. The completed initiation complex has the first donor already positioned.
Which statement about a leaderless bacterial mRNA is most defensible?
Its start codon lies at or near the 5′ end and some such messages recruit 70S directly
It must contain a conventional long SD leader
It never uses tRNA
It is always untranslated
Leaderless initiation is an alternative route and does not eliminate the need for a first donor. Factor and subunit requirements vary by system.
Which comparison is correct?
Bacterial IF2 is the same protein as eukaryotic eIF2
Bacterial IF2 is evolutionarily related to eukaryotic eIF5B
IF3 is the bacterial version of the full eIF3 complex
IF1 is a methionyl-tRNA synthetase
The bacterial IF2/eIF5B relationship illustrates why numbering is not a reliable homology guide. The other factors have distinct functions.
Which observation directly tests whether SD–aSD sequence complementarity contributes to recognition?
A mutant reporter has low protein output alone
A sample contains 70S particles
Restoring matching pairing through a compensatory rRNA mutation preferentially rescues the altered reporter
The transcript contains AUG
Specific compensatory rescue is a stronger test than a sequence observation or a single loss-of-function experiment. The rRNA and message must also be checked for other defects.
A peptide deformylase removes which group?
The entire initiator tRNA
All N-terminal methionines
The alpha carbon of methionine
The N-formyl group on the nascent protein
Deformylation removes the formyl group. A separate methionine aminopeptidase may subsequently remove the N-terminal methionine.
Which step consumes ATP to AMP?
Methionine aminoacylation
IF2 activation of hydrolysis
SD base pairing
50S docking itself
The synthetase activates the amino acid using ATP and releases AMP after transfer. IF2 uses GTP; RNA pairing and subunit contact are not ATP-to-AMP reactions.
Which statement best distinguishes a promoter from an RBS?
Both are necessarily identical sequences
A promoter directs transcription; an RBS helps recruit and position a translating ribosome
An RBS is exclusively DNA-bound RNA polymerase
A promoter forms the peptide bond
Promoters act at DNA transcription initiation, while ribosome-binding regions function on RNA. A DNA sequence encoding an RBS may be discussed genetically, but the ribosome recognizes the transcript.
Which property of initiator tRNA is not enough by itself to distinguish it from elongator methionine tRNA?
Acceptor-stem identity features
Preferential interaction with initiation machinery
CAU anticodon
Formylated aminoacyl end
Both methionine tRNAs commonly contain CAU. Distinct structural features and formylation help direct the correct tRNA to initiation.
What directly supplies the chemical driving potential for the first peptide-bond transfer?
Phosphorylation by IF3
Cleavage of 16S rRNA
GTP transfer onto peptide
Activated ester linkage of the aminoacyl donor
Charging produces an activated aminoacyl-tRNA ester. The GTP cycle coordinates factors rather than phosphorylating the peptide.
Which statement about bacterial polycistronic messages is correct?
Different coding regions can have different initiation efficiencies
All products must be synthesized in equal amounts
Only the first ORF can initiate
Each coding region necessarily has a separate transcription promoter
Local initiation signals can differ within one transcript. Translation of one cistron can also influence another, so equal RNA abundance does not imply equal output.
Which sedimentation claim is correct?
30S + 50S equals 80S by definition
70S is the sedimentation coefficient class of the associated bacterial particle
All 70S particles must be active initiation complexes
Svedberg is a unit of nucleotide count
Sedimentation depends on hydrodynamic properties, not a simple sum. Association alone does not prove correct start selection or catalytic readiness.
Which technique most directly localizes a stable initiation complex on a particular mRNA?
Measuring total protein mass
Measuring OD alone
Toeprinting with appropriate controls
Counting DNA copies
Toeprinting maps a reverse-transcription obstruction associated with a bound complex. It does not alone demonstrate formation of a full-length protein.
Which is a valid description of transcription–translation coupling?
The ribosome copies DNA directly
Every bacterial transcript is obligatorily translated
Ribosomes translate ahead of the newly synthesized RNA
A ribosome may initiate while RNA polymerase continues transcript synthesis
The accessible 5′ RNA can be translated before transcription is complete. The ribosome cannot translate nucleotides that do not yet exist.
Which statement about archaea is correct?
Their initiation factors are generally more closely related to eukaryotic initiation factors than to the complete bacterial IF set
All archaea use IF1/IF2/IF3 exactly as E. coli
Archaeal initiator Met is invariably formylated
Archaea have no ribosomes
Archaea have a distinct initiation apparatus and generally use unformylated initiator methionine. Some RNA recognition features overlap with bacteria.
Which observation is consistent with a slow IF2 maturation step?
Only DNA synthesis changes
Correct 30S occupancy and 70S association persist but first-dipeptide production decreases
All mRNA disappears necessarily
Peptide bonds form before large-subunit joining
Joined particles may remain in an intermediate state. Dipeptide formation is the more functional readout, though controls must exclude a catalytic defect.
Assertion: IF1 helps keep ordinary elongator tRNA from occupying A during initiation. Reason: IF1 interacts with the small-subunit A-site region.
Both true and reason explains assertion
Both true but unrelated
Assertion true; reason false
Assertion false
Its A-region interaction helps establish an initiation-specific state. The factor is released as the ribosome becomes available for elongation.
Assertion: Absence of fMet from a mature protein proves that its bacterial initiation was unformylated. Reason: Deformylase can remove the N-formyl group.
Both true
Assertion true; reason false
Assertion false; reason true
Both false
Post-initiation processing can remove the group, and sometimes the methionine. Mature protein sequence alone cannot establish the chemical state of the initial donor.
Which set of statements is correct? I. Initiation begins a reading frame. II. IF2 is a GTPase. III. All bacterial initiation requires SD. IV. A productive final complex contains the initiator at P.
I and III only
II and III only
III and IV only
I, II and IV only
I, II and IV describe the canonical functional requirements. III is false because leaderless and other SD-independent initiation routes occur.
Match IF1, IF2, IF3 to functions: X = A-region organization, Y = initiator/large-subunit coordination, Z = start selection/anti-association.
IF1–X, IF2–Y, IF3–Z
IF1–Y, IF2–Z, IF3–X
IF1–Z, IF2–X, IF3–Y
IF1–X, IF2–Z, IF3–Y
The first pairing is the correct summary of their predominant roles. The factors cooperate rather than operating as isolated enzymes.

Which combination is correct? I. SD pairs with rRNA. II. The start codon pairs with initiator tRNA. III. Formyltransferase directly uses GTP. IV. Peptide bond formation requires the large-subunit catalytic environment.
I and III
I, II and IV
II and III
III and IV
I and II distinguish two recognition duplexes. IV describes the catalytic requirement. Formyltransferase uses a folate-derived formyl donor, not GTP.
C: numerical
The sequence is 5′-AGGAGG-UUCAAC-AUG-GAA-UAA-3′. Assign the first and last SD nucleotides relative to A of AUG = +1; predict the primary translated chain.
The six spacer bases occupy −6 to −1; the SD occupies −12 through −7. AUG initiates fMet and GAA specifies Glu. The primary chain is fMet–Glu; UAA contributes no residue.
numerical
An initiation region has Kd 25 nM, another 100 nM. Free 30S is 100 nM. Estimate the occupancy of each and their ratio.
For a dilute ligand, f = [R]/([R]+Kd). Values are 100/125 = 0.8 and 100/200 = 0.5; ratio 1.6. This is binding occupancy, not a guaranteed protein-output ratio.
numerical
At RT = 2.5 kJ/mol a folded state lies 5 kJ/mol below an open state. Estimate the open fraction. What changes if ΔGfold becomes +2.5 kJ/mol?
Open fraction = 1/(1+exp(−ΔGfold/RT)). For −5, f = 1/(1+e²) = 0.119. For +2.5, f = 1/(1+e⁻¹) = 0.731. Accessibility increases roughly 6.14-fold under this two-state model.
numerical
An intermediate progresses at 6 s⁻¹ or dissociates at 2 s⁻¹. A mutant changes the rates to 3 s⁻¹ and 3 s⁻¹. Compare productive encounter probabilities.
Reference 6/(6+2) = 0.75. Mutant 3/(3+3) = 0.50. Relative productive probability is 2/3; this assumes competing independent first-order exits.
numerical
In a simplified reaction 750 initiations succeed with precharged fMet-tRNA. Count IF2 GTP and then include aminoacylation from free Met.
750 GTP molecules; adding charging consumes 750 ATP molecules to AMP, or 1500 phosphate equivalents. Total 2250 equivalents. Direct formyltransferase does not separately consume ATP.
numerical
A preparation consumes 3600 IF2-associated GTP molecules and yields 3000 productive initiation events. Calculate the mean GTP cost and excess relative to the ideal.
3600/3000 = 1.2 GTP per productive event. Excess = 600 GTP molecules; this is 20% above ideal, or one sixth of all measured hydrolysis. It does not localize the failed reactions.
numerical
A message initiates at 0.15 s⁻¹ and ribosomes remain for 40 s. A second condition gives 0.10 s⁻¹ and 70 s. Compare mean occupancy and output flux assuming no losses.
Jτ gives 6 versus 7 ribosomes. Completion flux is 0.15 versus 0.10 per second at steady state. Occupancy increased even though output decreased because residence time increased.
numerical
Reference produces 120 correct and 5 incorrect start events; mutant 125 correct and 25 incorrect. Calculate error fractions and their fold change.
Reference 5/125 = 4%; mutant 25/150 = 16.67%. Error fraction rises about 4.17-fold, despite a small increase in correct starts.
numerical
Reporter RNA falls from 100 to 40 units, production from 200 to 40 units per hour. Determine production per RNA and the relative change.
Reference 200/100 = 2; altered 40/40 = 1. Production per RNA halves. RNA abundance also falls by 60%; neither change alone accounts for all of the output reduction.
numerical
RNA polymerase progresses at 60 nt/s and a ribosome at 15 codons/s. Under a constant-rate model, how much does separation grow in 12 s?
15 codons/s = 45 nt/s. Difference = 15 nt/s; growth = 180 nt over 12 s. Real coupling and pauses can alter the distance.
experimental
A four-way SD rescue assay yields outputs WT/WT 100, mutant mRNA/WT ribosome 8, WT mRNA/mutant ribosome 10, mutant/mutant 70. Interpret and identify controls.

The matched double mutant gives 8.75-fold rescue relative to the first mismatch and 70% of reference. Specific rescue supports pairing; check RNA abundance, ribosome assembly, folding and unrelated translation.
experimental
An IF2 mutant gives normal 30S toeprints, normal 70S sedimentation but little dipeptide. A wild-type IF2 restores product. What defect is supported?

A defect after early start selection and joining is consistent, such as delayed GTP-dependent maturation. Directly measure GTP hydrolysis, IF2 retention and catalytic competence to distinguish these possibilities.
experimental
A second IF2 mutant gives weak 30S start signals but normal hydrolysis in a separate activated-GTPase assay. Why can whole-reaction hydrolysis still be reduced?
Few productive complexes reach the activation state. An intact intrinsic catalytic ability does not imply normal initiation-complex assembly; compare initiator binding and subunit docking.
experimental
An IF3 variant raises both canonical and alternative start occupancy, but alternative protein yield rises disproportionately. Explain.

Loss of discrimination can increase incorrect starts without reducing total throughput. Use site-specific product mapping and no-ribosome toeprint controls to confirm the alternative start rather than elongation errors.
experimental
A start-region mutation leaves SD pairing intact but changes AUG to a poorly accepted triplet. Bulk RNA binding is preserved; stable start-site signal falls. Why?
Upstream recruitment remains possible; codon–anticodon selection or subsequent stabilization fails. Binding assays that do not resolve positions may obscure the defect.
experimental

A reporter with exposed SD and one with the same SD trapped in a hairpin have identical transcript abundance. A compensatory stem-disrupting substitution restores expression without changing SD. What is supported?

Accessibility contributes independently of SD identity. The substitution may change other interactions, so assess RNA structure and initiation-complex occupancy rather than inferring the exact folding energy from protein yield.
experimental
In a toeprinting assay start sites are at positions 30 and 75. A validated +16 offset applies. A mutant has bands at 46 and 91; the no-ribosome sample also has a band at 91. Interpret.

46 is compatible with the first start. The 91 band is ambiguous because naked RNA can produce it. Compare ribosome-dependent band intensity, start mutants and product mapping before claiming a second start.
experimental
A formyltransferase mutant has normal Met-tRNA charging but reduced formylated tRNA and impaired translation. Would adding more MetRS necessarily correct the problem?
No. The defective step is after charging. Extra MetRS cannot substitute for transferase. Restoring normal transferase or testing unformylated initiation addresses the proposed causal step.
experimental
A tRNA anticodon remains CAU but a change in its acceptor stem reduces formylation. Why might normal AUG pairing not rescue initiation?
The anticodon checks the triplet, but identity elements influence formyltransferase recognition and routing through IF2. Correct pairing alone cannot restore a missing chemical or structural feature.
experimental
A bacterial protein purified at maturity starts with Ala, although its gene has AUG-GCU. Explain without invoking a code change.

Initiation can install fMet, then incorporate Ala. Deformylase removes the formyl group and methionine aminopeptidase can remove the initial Met when substrate context permits. Mature Ala is consistent with post-initiation processing.
experimental
An aSD mutation inhibits a conventional leader-containing reporter but has little effect on a reporter beginning at AUG. Is the second reporter necessarily independent of IF2?
No. The experiment only challenges a particular RNA-pairing route. The leaderless reporter may still require initiator selection and IF2-dependent functions; factor-specific tests are necessary.
experimental

A premature stop in an upstream cistron reduces downstream expression. A stem-disrupting mutation recovers downstream expression even though upstream translation remains interrupted. What mechanism is supported?

Translation of the upstream ORF may normally expose the downstream initiation region by disrupting a stem. Rescue supports accessibility rather than an absolute need for an upstream ribosome; verify RNA abundance and structure.
experimental
Increasing Mg²⁺ raises the fraction of 70S material but reduces correct protein output. Give a mechanistic explanation and a discriminating experiment.

Ionic stabilization may favor nonproductive or prematurely joined states. Measure start-site occupancy, factor retention and first-dipeptide yield at matched conditions. High 70S abundance alone is not evidence of successful initiation.
experimental
A mutation reduces final reporter protein but the short-pulse synthesis rate and transcript abundance remain normal. Where should the investigation focus?

Protein turnover or maturation is a plausible cause. Initiation is not demonstrated to be defective by final abundance; compare protein stability and direct activity, while allowing for assay sensitivity.
experimental
An archaeal extract supports translation of a leaderless transcript with unformylated Met-tRNAi. A student claims bacterial IF1, IF2, IF3 must therefore be present. Evaluate.

The conclusion confuses similar outcomes with identical mechanisms. Archaea have a distinct initiation-factor ensemble closer to eukaryotic counterparts. Leaderlessness and a 70S class do not establish bacterial factor identity or formylation.
